PDA derivation and syscall handlers for creating and finding program addresses.

# Purpose
This file implements VM syscall support for Solana program derived address, or `PDA`, creation and search. It contains the core helper [`fd_vm_derive_pda`](<#fd_vm_derive_pda>), which hashes the seed list, optional bump seed, program id, and the `ProgramDerivedAddress` marker, then checks that the result is not a valid ed25519 curve point. It also contains [`fd_vm_translate_and_check_program_address_inputs`](<#fd_vm_translate_and_check_program_address_inputs>), which reads seed metadata and program id values from VM memory, performs bounds and size checks, and translates VM addresses into host addresses for later use.

The file also defines the syscall entry points [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_create_program_address`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_create_program_address>) and [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_try_find_program_address`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_try_find_program_address>). [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_create_program_address`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_create_program_address>) derives one PDA and writes it to VM memory if the result is valid. [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_try_find_program_address`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_try_find_program_address>) repeats the derivation with bump seeds from `255` down to `1` until it finds a valid PDA, then writes both the PDA and the bump seed back to VM memory. Both syscalls update compute units and return Solana-style error codes for invalid seeds, invalid PDAs, and memory access failures.
